title: Scout: repo-map of the CLI and status path for eval 001
spec: Skill repo-map. Question: where does `orchestrator status` produce its output, what does Pool().status() return per account and for codex (field names, types), and how are CLI subcommands and their tests structured? Cite path:line for: the status branch in orchestrator/cli.py, Pool.status in orchestrator/pool.py, the existing CLI test (if any) in tests/test_orchestrator.py, and the test harness conventions (TMP, ORCH_ROOT). Suggest the smallest place to add a `--plain` flag printing one line per account and one for codex. Max 8 findings.
acceptance: findings cite path:line for cli status branch, Pool.status fields, test conventions
suggested_next names the exact insertion point for --plain
JSON schema of the scout prompt respected

findings.claim: The `status` CLI branch calls Pool().status(), merges in a queue dict keyed by bus status, and dumps as pretty JSON (indent=1). This is the sole place status output is produced today.

Pool.status() returns {'accounts': [...], 'codex': {...}}. Each account dict has: id:str, utilization:float(round 3), day_tokens:int, daily_budget:int, cooling_s:int(>=0), reason:str (from Account.hold_reason).

Pool.status()'s codex dict has: available:bool (from codex_available()), running:int, day_tasks:int, cooling_s:int(>=0), on_exhausted:str (a config string literal: 'hold'|'fallback_claude'|'overflow_api').

There is no existing CLI-level test for orchestrator/cli.py or the status command. tests/test_orchestrator.py imports only bus, pool (as P), spawn, merge, executor directly — cli is never imported or invoked as a module; cli.py only appears as a string path inside hook-guardrail test payloads.

Test harness convention: a module-level TMP dir is created via tempfile.mkdtemp, exported as ORCH_ROOT env var before any orchestrator import, then seeded with a copied pool.toml and symlinked prompts/.claude dirs; sys.path is prepended with REPO so `from orchestrator import ...` resolves against the source tree, not an installed package.

CLI subcommands follow a uniform argparse pattern: each verb is sub.add_parser(name) with .add_argument(...) chained inline (e.g. resume/hold/merge/post), dispatched via a flat if/elif chain on a.cmd in main(); output for stateful commands is always json.dumps(..., indent=1).

Smallest insertion point for --plain: add `.add_argument('--plain', action='store_true')` to the existing `sub.add_parser('status')` call at cli.py:22, then branch inside the `if a.cmd == 'status':` block at cli.py:30-31 — on a.plain, iterate Pool().status()['accounts'] printing one f-string line per account (id, utilization, cooling_s, reason) and one final line for the 'codex' dict (available, running, day_tasks, cooling_s); otherwise keep the current json.dumps path unchanged.

No test currently exercises cli.py's argparse wiring or output formatting at all, so a --plain test would be new coverage, not a modification of an existing test — likely added as a new TestCase class in tests/test_orchestrator.py following the TMP/ORCH_ROOT pattern, invoking orchestrator.cli.main() with patched sys.argv or capturing stdout.

open_questions: Is stdout capture (capsys-style) or subprocess invocation the intended way to test cli.main() in this codebase, given no precedent test does either?
suggested_next: Add `.add_argument('--plain', action='store_true')` to `sub.add_parser('status')` at orchestrator/cli.py:22, and branch on `a.plain` inside the `if a.cmd == 'status':` block at orchestrator/cli.py:30-31 to print one line per account plus one for codex, falling back to the existing json.dumps for the non-plain path.
